audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may double-count customer prepayments
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; $1,102.591m cash/STI was added while filed deferred revenue was $1,277.646m
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash bridge may add operating working-capital funding as surplus cash while forecast OE includes earnings and fulfillment costs associated with the prepaid contracts.
audit_findings.evidence: For both aligners and scanners, we usually collect the total consideration owed prior to all performance obligations being satisfied with payment terms generally varying from net 30 to net 180 days.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that customer billings precede fulfillment and that deferred revenue exceeds the entire cash addition. It does not identify which dollars remain necessary for fulfillment or normal liquidity, so the actual duplication is unresolved. The exposed cash bridge equals $15.03 per share and 13.1% of base equity value, making the issue reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation range.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 cash to deferred-revenue funding, forecast fulfillment costs, contract assets, and minimum operating cash; rerun every scenario with only demonstrably excess cash in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may understate ongoing capital requirements
audit_findings.magnitude: $22.6m-$47.6m annual capex increase versus FY2025; if entirely maintenance, computed base-value reduction is $317.6m-$668.8m or $4.33-$9.12 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher normalized maintenance capex reduces annual owner earnings and therefore both explicit-period cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect our investments in capital expenditures to be between $125 million and $150 million for the next 12 months.
audit_findings.explanation: FY2025 capex was $102.4m, versus filed 2026 guidance of $125m-$150m; first-half 2026 spending of $66.45m annualizes to $132.9m. The increase is demonstrated, but the record does not separate maintenance spending from growth capacity, technology upgrades, or the new India project. Consequently, the valuation effect may be material but cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain project-level 2026 capex and management's maintenance-versus-growth classification, normalize maintenance capex, and rerun OE and all scenarios using the supported amount.

audit_findings.title: The UK VAT appeal creates an unquantified claim on cash and margins
audit_findings.magnitude: $37.5m accrued claim, or $0.51 per share; recurring UK margin effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The accrued claim should reduce the equity bridge if unpaid, while prospective VAT that cannot be passed through reduces revenue, margins, and OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In August 2025, we stopped charging VAT to our United Kingdom customers.
audit_findings.explanation: This is no longer merely a possible appeal exposure: the Upper Tribunal ruled against Align and the June 2026 filing recorded a $37.5m liability. That recorded claim alone is only 0.45% of base equity value and cannot materially change the conclusion. However, Align stopped charging customers VAT in August 2025, and the record gives no UK sales or pass-through data with which to quantify the potentially recurring margin effect.
audit_findings.action: Deduct any unpaid $37.5m accrual from the bridge, obtain post-August-2025 UK taxable sales and pricing/pass-through evidence, and rerun OE margins under upheld and successful-appeal outcomes.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified litigation could rank ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $31.8m accrued at June 2026, or $0.43 per share; remaining exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpaid settlements or judgments reduce the equity bridge; recurring legal costs, business restrictions, damages, or licensing obligations reduce OE or growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We are currently unable to predict the outcome of these lawsuits and therefore we cannot determine the likelihood of loss, if any, nor estimate a range of possible loss.
audit_findings.explanation: The June filing demonstrates a $31.8m accrued legal settlement, equal to only 0.38% of base equity value by itself. The Straumann jury rejected the asserted counterclaims, but post-trial motions and appeals remain possible; the antitrust appeals and Angelalign proceedings also remain unresolved without loss ranges. The filed record therefore establishes a small current claim but cannot establish the materiality of the remaining exposure.
audit_findings.action: Deduct unpaid accrued settlements from the bridge and update court dockets, post-trial motions, appeals, insurance coverage, claimed damages, potential injunctions, and any reasonably possible loss ranges before rerunning affected scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Previously accrued uncertain taxes may be omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $120.9m gross unrecognized tax benefits; $1.65 per share if fully deducted
audit_findings.mechanism: A historical-period tax liability whose expense has already reduced earnings should be deducted from gross cash in the equity bridge when its eventual cash settlement is not captured in forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The total amount of gross unrecognized tax benefits as of December 31, 2025 was $ 117.4 million, of which $ 111.9 million would impact our effective tax rate if recognized.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing reports $120.9m of gross unrecognized tax benefits, but does not identify the exact cash-settlement liability within income-tax payable and other liabilities. Even conservatively deducting the entire gross amount would reduce base value by only 1.44%, from $114.44 to about $112.79 per share, versus the $158.635 market price. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion on the supplied scale.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $120.9m gross position to the $69.964m income-tax payable, other long-term liabilities, related deferred taxes, and expected settlement amounts; deduct only the confirmed debt-like cash claim.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $80.1m FY2020 residual; $0 effect on the current $490m anchor under the stated MIN(trend, latest) rule
audit_findings.mechanism: Any eligible residual D&A add-back would increase historical OE and possibly the calculated trend, but it does not alter shares or the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2020 $80.1m (85.7% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The uncertainty is conservative because the residual was left as an expense. It concerns FY2020, while the valuation anchors to FY2025 OE of $490m because the $530m trend is already higher. Increasing FY2020 OE cannot raise the anchor under the stated rule, so it has no effect on the current valuation.
audit_findings.action: Classify the FY2020 residual from filed depreciation and amortization disclosures; rerun the historical series for documentation, while retaining the $490m anchor unless current-year evidence independently changes it.
